resources.string: Hoverboard Remote needs Bluetooth access to scan for and connect to your board. This is required to drive the vehicle. No location data is collected.
The board would not attach. It may be armed; power-cycle it and try again.
Hold the throttle to drive · release to stop
Tap ARM to enable the motors
Bound: both boards get this demand · release to stop
Rider requirement waived: in balance mode, arming engages. Hold the frame upright when arming.
Rider requirement may be waived: the app cannot tell what the board is running. In balance mode, arming may engage. Hold the frame upright when arming.
Fault reporting is not implemented in the firmware this app was built for, so this cannot warn you.
Not measured. The firmware sends a fixed 36.0 V; no board senses its pack yet.
The slave does not report its rider level
%1$s. The rider requirement may be waived on this board, so the board may run Profile A whatever the pads say: this may not be the rider level it acts on.
Rider not required on this board: Profile A always runs
The slave\'s profiles follow the rider requirement read from its store, taken to be what it runs: the board does not report the value it booted with.
These are the values last read from this board. Writes are off until it is read again.
~ converging: the loop reaches the staged value within %1$s s of the change, while it runs
Staged: the board\'s RAM value, which this slider writes. The running loop ramps to it.
Engaged: what the balance loop is using now. The board does not report it; it converges to staged over time and never jumps while the loop runs.
Flash: what a reboot restores. Only Save writes it.
~ converging: the ramp\'s bound since the last change has not elapsed. A bound, not a reading.
* unsaved: staged differs from flash. A reboot reverts to flash.
After each engage the loop starts with kp and bk at staged and ramps pr up from 0, within %1$s s. The board does not report when it engages.
Save writes flash, which the board refuses while armed. The sliders and Revert work armed.
Save is refused while armed. Disarm on the Ride tab first.
The board refused %1$s: outside the range it accepts.
The board does not know %1$s as a tunable gain (its firmware may predate the tune lane).

No answer about %1$s. The board may be out of reach, or its firmware may predate the tune lane.

resources.string: The stored IMU orientation is not a proper rotation, or part of it cannot be read while some of it was just written. That happens when an Apply wrote only part of a frame, and a board can also hold such a frame from before this session. A board powered up on it refuses to bring up its IMU, so it cannot balance. Pick a pose and Apply it; the power-cycle instruction comes back once the stored frame is whole.
The link drops when the board powers off; this unlocks then.
The Bluetooth module takes a new name only after it is power-cycled out of data mode.
Set by the link walk; not editable here.
The firmware currently drives six-step whatever is stored here.
0 = unset. A configured gate group needs %1$d DTG ticks or more.
The firmware converts this through the board\'s own counts per amp, then lowers a limit above what that board\'s sense range can hold, and raises one below its sense noise.
Not required: balance engages without a rider, so arming is the engage act and the frame must be held upright when arming. Profile A runs. Any byte but 0 reads as required.
0 = none. Refuses a balance engage below it, never ends a run.
The largest value the Tune steppers and the board accept for this gain, in both profiles; the minimum is 0. A stored gain above it is clamped at boot. Applies after a power-cycle.
Rail centivolts = count × slope / 10000 + offset. The firmware clamps the slope to 10000 to 32000 and the offset to -500 to 500 at boot.
1 = X, 2 = Y, 3 = Z, 0 = unset (the compiled role). Written only by the orientation pose picker above, together with the signs.
-1, +1, or 0 for unset (runs the firmware fallback for that axis). Every Apply checks the whole map is a rotation.
Stand the frame level, then set. The trims that zero the current pitch and roll go in the basket; Apply stores them.
No attitude from the board yet

Pick how the board sits in the machine: which face points up, then what points forward. The app writes both orientation fields from that choice: the axis roles (which chip axis is up, which measures the pitch rate) and the six signs. Every pose is a proper rotation; the board refuses any other frame at boot and does not bring up its IMU.

The poses assume the standard board family\'s chip mount (the measured yaw, not the firmware\'s compiled fallback). A board of another family needs its chip mount measured before these poses are right for it.
Stored as: %1$s. The board runs the stored map from its next power-up, not now.
Unset signs and roles run the firmware fallback.
The stored frame is not a proper rotation (mirrored, or an invalid pair of roles). The board refuses it at boot and does not bring up its IMU. Pick a pose below before it is next powered up.
Drawn with the machine\'s forward to the right and up at the top; the component side is shaded and the arrow marks the stock-forward edge.
unset (firmware fallback; reads as %1$s on this family)
The board as it runs now
Side view (forward to the right) and view from behind, tilted by the pitch and roll the board reports. Tilt the board: the drawing should tilt the same way. It shows the frame the board booted with.

Run on the assembled frame, after the power-cycle that applies the orientation. A pass means the pitch and roll the board reports agree with its map. The up-axis gravity sign and the pitch-rate sign are not sent over Bluetooth; they need the bench check.
Frame level: pitch and roll within 10° of zero.
Hold the frame leaning forward more than 10°: pitch reads negative.
The orientation is pending or staged. Apply it and power-cycle the board first.
Armed: nothing was changed. Disarm on the Ride tab to edit.
The board refused %1$s: it is armed.
The board stores %1$s as a different type.
The board could not store %1$s (flash full or failed).
%1$s: wrote %2$s but the board stores %3$s. Read again to see what it holds.
%1$s: no answer from the board. It was read again to see what it holds.
%1$s: the answer from the board could not be understood.
The link is busy with another read, so nothing was written; try again.
No board is attached, so nothing was sent.
A sign must be -1, 0 (unset) or +1. Nothing was written.
The accelerometer signs would form a mirrored frame (determinant -1). Nothing was written.
The gyro signs would form a mirrored frame (determinant -1). Nothing was written.
A sign or axis role is neither stored nor staged, so the frame cannot be checked. Read again first.
The axis roles would name one chip axis twice or a value outside 0 to 3. Nothing was written.
No attitude has arrived from the board yet.
The stored values this needs have not been read.
The board is running a value the app cannot know: a field this depends on is pending or staged. Apply and power-cycle first.
A different board attached. The edits for board %1$s were dropped.
A layout is written to flash, which the board refuses while armed. Disarm to edit it.
The layout has not been read yet.
%1$d of the layout\'s fields could not be read, so there is no layout to judge. Read again.
Part: %1$s, as the board reports it.
This board has not sent its part. Firmware from before the part was on the wire never does.
This board reports a part this app does not know.
A layout is only valid or invalid ON a part: pins that one part bonds the next one does not. So there is no verdict here, and nothing can be changed.

Applying one is the normal case: a preset is a whole layout for a board variant, so no pin has to be entered by hand. Drive direction, align offset and the current calibration are left as this board holds them: a pin map cannot state them.
This preset moves the power latch

The board holds its own power on through %1$s; this preset says %2$s. On battery, the pin is what keeps the board alive: if the wrong one is staged, the board powers itself off the moment it boots, and only a debugger attached over SWD can bring it back. Everything else in the preset is staged either way.
This layout validates. The board would accept it and bring up what it describes.
The layout has not been read, so there is nothing to judge.
This is not a guess. The board\'s boot validator is a pure function of these fields, this part and the reserved pins, and this is that function\'s answer.

What only a reboot can tell: whether the hardware behaves, so whether the IMU answers on the staged bus, the halls read and the motors turn. The board\'s own verdict is not readable over the link either, so a clean apply is confirmed by the board behaving on reconnect.
A wrong layout disables the affected function until it is corrected and re-booted; the board stays reachable. The link\'s own pins are not layout fields and cannot be claimed by one.
The board currently STORES a layout it would refuse, on %1$s. A layout is one object, so this is an invalid board rather than a board half-way to a new layout. Finish applying the changes below.
Apply is disabled while the verdict is a refusal. There is no override: the board would refuse this layout at boot and come up link-only.
No changes staged. Edits here are local until Apply writes them.
Power-cycle the board to apply %1$d field(s). The layout is read once at boot.
Waiting for the link to drop: a power-cycle takes the Bluetooth module down with the board.
Written, not applied: runs from the next power-up.
Direction and align offset are the Setup screen\'s rows. They are read here because a layout is one object, and they do not change the verdict.
Not editable here. On battery this pin is what holds the board\'s own power on, so a wrong one powers the board off at boot and only SWD can recover it.
Both pins and a model, or none: a half-staged IMU is a refused layout, not an absent IMU.
All six gates with a dead time at or above the floor, or none. The picker offers only this part\'s advanced-timer pins, and the six still have to form one timer\'s complementary set.
Both pins exactly when the sense is declared present, and both on an analog pin.
%1$d DTG ticks or more once the gates are configured; 0 only with them unset. A shorter one lets both FETs of a leg conduct.
This field could not be read.
Not editable: the board\'s part is not known.
No pin on this part is free and eligible for this function.
That byte is not a pin this encoding defines.
The function\'s fields are all-or-none and only some are set.
The gates are configured, so the dead time must be %1$d DTG ticks or more. Anything shorter is shoot-through.
%1$s is already claimed by another function.
%1$s belongs to a live link port or to SWD.
%1$s is not bonded on this part.
%1$s drives an advanced timer, so only a gate may claim it.
These six pins are not one advanced timer\'s complementary set.
%1$s has no ADC channel behind it.
Those two pins are not a hardware I2C bus. A software bus is not built.
The stored IMU orientation is not a rotation. The Setup screen owns it.
